text:
mia: Heads up — seeing broken span links when gateway serves responses from KV cache. Spans up to gateway look fine but worker/generator spans are orphaned.
sam: ugh. any pattern? batching, async queues, or specific routes?
mia: appears when request hits gateway, gateway returns cached payload without making downstream call. We still emit a small local span for cache hit. But when downstream worker later picks up the job (for side-effects) the trace isn't stitched. We currently only forward X-Redwood-Trace (opaque) on HTTP -> worker via message attribute, and rely on gateway setting Traceparent on the HTTP path. Problem: opaque header gets stripped on SNS -> lambda/kafka consumers and we lose parent id. Example headers seen on gateway logs:
```
Traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
baggage: s_id=kv-14;host=gateway-02
X-Redwood-Trace: rw-ctx=eyJwYXJlbnQiOiIweC0... (opaque, base64)
```
When gateway returns cached payload we still emit span id 00f0... but don't create an entry in trace backend that links to the downstream worker span because the worker only sees the message attribute rw-ctx sometimes encoded as binary.
olivia: This rings a bell — we had a similar mismatch when we switched to batched consumer mode. Kafka client libs convert message headers into a byte array and our rw-ctx header is sometimes truncated when inserted as a binary header.
aj: Are we using W3C traceparent or keeping the custom rw-ctx for correlation? We should standardize on traceparent + tracestate for cross-process continuity and keep rw-ctx as best-effort fallback.
mia: We're emitting both currently, but in a few paths (gateway cache fast-path) we only write rw-ctx to message attributes and not traceparent. Gateway fast-path is a lightweight handler that doesn't run full middleware (to keep latency <3ms) so it skips the normal OTEL instrumentation which sets traceparent. It does set rw-ctx to avoid surface-level loss but that's not surviving queue transports.
sam: Options:
- make fast-path add traceparent header (adds cost/latency risk)
- switch rw-ctx to base64-encoded JSON and ensure consumers decode (compat risk)
- use a compact header that fits existing binary header size limits and avoid truncation (tight)
- attach a small correlation id in message key and persist in KV for later lookup (adds read cost)

olivia: Also need to handle sampling mismatches. If gateway sampled=false but worker is sampled=true, we might get partial traces that look like different roots. Need to propagate sampling bit explicitly in headers.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: middleware/trace-fastpath  -> canary to 10% gateway instances at 2026-03-24T03:00Z
aj: Proposal: 1) fast-path will write W3C traceparent and a minimal tracestate entry (rw=s:0/1 plus baker id), without full OTEL span creation; 2) rw-ctx stays as backup but we compress it to 12 bytes (parentSpanId + sampling + flags) to avoid header truncation; 3) consumers (workers) will prefer traceparent but fall back to rw-ctx when traceparent missing; 4) add a small router-level stitcher that on job pickup looks for correlation header and re-attaches traceparent before downstream calls.
mia: I like 1+3+4. Concern about adding traceparent to fast-path: we've tested microbenchmarks, it adds ~0.7ms p50. Still within SLO, but need load testing for p99.
sam: If we compress rw-ctx to 12 bytes, we need a deterministic encoding. Suggest: 8 bytes parent_span_id (last 8 of 16) + 1 byte sampling + 1 byte flags + 2 bytes reserved CRC. base64 of 12 bytes fits typical header limits.
olivia: Consumer change is small: prefer traceparent parse using otel API; if absent, parse rw-ctx and create fake traceparent (same version format). Also set span.kind=consumer for stitching.
aj: Edge case: batch consumers that join multiple messages — when multiple messages have different traceparents, we should create a parent 'batch' root and attach individual message spans as children, preserving original parentSpanId as remote parent via links. Otherwise traces will interleave and look wrong.
mia: Good call. For batch handler API we can pass an array of parent ids and emit links. Implementation task list:
- gateway/fastpath: emit traceparent + compact rw-ctx (owner: mia)
- worker lib: parse traceparent || rw-ctx, support links for batch (owner: aj)
- infra: canary rollout + load test (owner: sam)
- telemetry: update exporter to tag stitched spans with "stitch.source=kvcache-fastpath" for queries (owner: olivia)

aj: I'll add unit tests to ensure binary header survives kafka/java client roundtrip. Also add an integration that replays cached-vs-live path to compare trace linking.
sam: can we also add a kibana alert for "orphaned spans rate" increase > 0.5%? olivia will need that metric renamed in dashboards.
olivia: yep will add alert and update per-route trace view. Also add evals to Redwood Optimize to measure quality regressions when we stitch vs not.
mia: ok I'll open PRs for gateway change + docs on header format. thanks team :thumbsup:
sam: :eyes: watching the canary logs
infra-bot: canary deploy started for middleware/trace-fastpath on 10% of instances at 2026-03-24T03:05Z
mia: will follow up with perf numbers after 1h of traffic.
